subject: No Vibes Allowed: Building a Smart Memory System for AI Agents
body:
Hey First Name,

Hope you're having a great week! Our latest 🦄 ai that works session was a deep dive into "No Vibes Allowed: Building a Smart Memory System for AI Agents."

If you missed it, or want to revisit anything, you can find the full recording, code, and diagrams on GitHub right here:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We packed a lot into the session, exploring how to build a smart, volume-based memory system (we call them Context Shards) for AI agents, and the collaborative product engineering process that made it happen. Here's a quick rundown:

*   **Context Shards: Our Smart Memory System**: We really dug into how we built 'Context Shards.' This is a volume-based memory system for AI agents designed to learn from repeated user interactions across a team. The goal? To cut down on all those irrelevant, aggressively added memories that often clog up AI systems.
*   **Iterative Product Design & Human Feedback**: We walked through our product discovery process, from initial Figma mocks all the way to high-fidelity prototypes. A key takeaway was the importance of early user feedback and keeping a 'human-in-the-loop' to whitelist and refine the memories our AI agents generate.
*   **Specialized Supervisor Agents for Smart Workflows**: We showed how we designed specialized supervisor agents. These agents have different jobs and cost profiles (think cron-triggered batch processing versus instant Slack responses). They're crucial for identifying and injecting the right context into the main agent loop, which ultimately makes the AI more effective and a lot smoother to use.

If there's one big takeaway from the session, it's this:
Building truly effective AI features, like a memory system for your whole team, isn't just about the tech. It really comes down to a disciplined, iterative product engineering process. You need to prioritize early user feedback, strategically use specialized AI agents, and adopt a 'burn the tokens' mentality. That means quickly figuring out what delivers value before you start optimizing for cost.

Got questions? Just hit reply to this email or hop into our Discord:
https://www.boundaryml.com/discord
We genuinely read every message!

Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
